The bus sighs at the corner, releasing weary passengers home.
Windows on the bus reflect faces made of blue evening.
The driver hums a road only wheels can hear plainly.
I ride to the end because the city surprises me.
Neon signs blink their colorful opinions there on wet pavement.
Rain makes the asphalt into a dark shining river below.
Umbrellas bloom like mushrooms along the crowded busy evening street.
A saxophone spills gold notes from an open doorway nearby.
People hurry, but music softly catches their shoulders gently anyway.
The night market smells of spice, warm smoke, and laughter.
Lanterns swing above heads like friendly planets hanging low tonight.
Children always chase bubbles, and bubbles chase the wind upward.
A vendor folds newspapers into small blue boats of tomorrow.
Coins become seeds when given with a warm open hand.

Stars appear as pinholes in the dark tent above us.
The moon watches the city with one calm silver eye.
A late bird crosses the sky and disappears completely soon.
I think about how quiet can be a vast country.
Its roads are pauses, its rivers are slow deep breathing.
Every heart carries a map drawn by invisible inner weather.
Love is often the lantern that makes shadows less frightening.
Hope is the door left slightly open for early morning.
